summary: Validated the Vercel uv/pyproject.toml deploy-manifest fix. Created /app/backend/tests/test_uv_pyproject.py with 16 tests covering pyproject.toml schema, uv.lock header + locked packages, `uv lock --check`, `uv sync --frozen` (with .venv cleanup), version-pin compatibility with requirements.txt, and vercel.json backend service. All 16 tests PASSED. Backend regression via curl: admin login -> 200 with token, /api/wallet/balance -> 200 with numeric balance (0.0), /api/operators -> 200 with 4 categories (mobile_prepaid, dth, electricity, data_card). /app/backend/.venv is absent (properly cleaned).

minor.issue: Iteration 6 test test_vercel_deploy_config.py::TestVercelManifest::test_frontend_service_config asserts buildCommand == 'yarn build' but iteration 7 intentionally changed it to 'CI=false yarn build'. Pre-existing test assertion needs updating; production behavior is correct (yarn is still used, CI=false only suppresses CRA warnings-as-errors). Not caused by this iteration.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Update /app/backend/tests/test_vercel_deploy_config.py::test_frontend_service_config to accept 'CI=false yarn build' (or any command containing 'yarn build' + no 'npm'). Pre-existing, not blocking this deploy fix.
critical_code_review_comments: pyproject.toml correctly declares dep-only workspace via [tool.uv].package = false — no accidental sdist build on Vercel.

requirements.txt still contains dev/build-only packages (pytest, black, isort, flake8, mypy, boto3, pandas, numpy, emergentintegrations) that are NOT in pyproject.toml. This is intentional: Vercel uses pyproject.toml for runtime install and skipping those keeps cold-start slim. But it means anyone doing `pip install -r requirements.txt` locally gets more than `uv sync` gets on Vercel. Consider documenting this divergence in a README note.

uv.lock resolved pydantic 2.13.4 (>= 2.6.4 from pyproject) — much newer than any pin. This is fine because bcrypt/fastapi versions are hard-pinned, but future `uv lock` runs may drift pydantic-core. Acceptable for now.

email-validator, python-multipart, tzdata are declared in pyproject.toml but server.py must actually import/use them at runtime — spot check confirms email-validator is transitively required by pydantic EmailStr, python-multipart by FastAPI form handling. All good.

success_rate.backend: 100% (16/16 iteration-scoped tests + backend endpoint regression via curl)

seed_data_creation: None. .venv created during uv sync test was cleaned up (rm -rf /app/backend/.venv).
context_for_next_testing_agent: The Vercel uv-deploy fix (pyproject.toml + uv.lock in /app/backend) is validated end-to-end. `uv lock --check` and `uv sync --frozen` both succeed from a clean state. Next testing agent should reuse /app/backend/tests/test_uv_pyproject.py as a regression guard whenever backend deps change. Also note: iteration 6's test_frontend_service_config has stale assertion for buildCommand — update to substring check ('yarn build' in cmd) to unblock CI while keeping the anti-npm guard.
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: Vercel's Python services runtime uses `uv` (not pip) and requires a pyproject.toml + uv.lock at the service root. Backend only had requirements.txt → `uv lock` failed → deploy aborted. Fix: added minimal pyproject.toml declaring the 12 runtime deps (with [tool.uv].package=false to mark as dep-only workspace) plus a generated uv.lock resolving 27 packages. Verified locally that `uv lock --check` reports no drift and `uv sync --frozen` installs a working env (fastapi, motor, pymongo, pydantic all present). No changes to server.py, vercel.json, or the running supervisor backend.
